claims.text: Greg Lavecchia (co-founder and CEO of Bloom) asserts that the people who win are not the people who show up when they feel motivated, but rather those who show up consistently regardless of motivation. This frames consistency as the decisive competitive variable separating winners from non-winners in entrepreneurship.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia

claims.text: Greg Lavecchia (co-founder and CEO of Bloom) asserts that every entrepreneur others look up to did not begin with experience or a track record on day one. Lavecchia applies this to himself directly, noting he had a negative track record when he started, making track record a non-prerequisite for entrepreneurial entry.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia

claims.text: Greg Lavecchia (co-founder and CEO of Bloom) asserts that entrepreneurship begins by taking on one small battle at a time, not by having a grand vision from the start. Lavecchia describes his own entry point as simply wanting to do something, not the specific goal of building the largest energy drink brand in the country.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia
conditions: early-stage entrepreneurship with no prior track record

examples.text: Greg Lavecchia used his own founding of Bloom as an example of track-record-free entrepreneurship: he had a negative track record at the outset and did not start with a goal to build the largest energy drink in the country. He started by answering Instagram questions from his audience, framing his path as a series of small battles rather than a grand plan.

practices.text: Show up consistently regardless of motivation; winners are defined by presence under low motivation, not high motivation.
Start entrepreneurship by taking on one small battle rather than waiting until you have experience or a track record.
